note: Identity case inputs for Front (F-1 with Codex's K-3236). Authored from the law, before lowerModuleDefinitions exists. A definition row is its declaration kind (tsts node kind) and its path of [name, ordinal] segments from the module; rows of a file are in the syntax tree's preorder. An export or use group lists [file, path] pairs in canonical order (a bare path where the group is in the same file). A repeated capture of any case must give identical identities: that is a property of a run, asserted where these inputs are run, not a row here. Added after R2's review of W5-4 and K-3250: every source is parsed by the checker in the checking case, and the declaration nodes it finds must equal the rows, kind by kind in preorder; The readings of K-3268 are applied: a pattern-holding parameter has an identity, a pattern-holding variable declaration or binding element has none, an export assignment always has its node's identity, and an authored namespace export is a declaration.

cases.name: enum-and-type-parameters
cases.rule: F-1: EnumDeclaration, EnumMember and TypeParameter are declarations with identities, owned like any member; a parameter property is one Parameter
cases.note: constructor(readonly value: T) is one Parameter node with one row, under the constructor. That node is also what declares the class member value, so the member's declaration identity is Box#0/#0/value#0, not Box#0/value#0

cases.name: binding-elements
cases.rule: K-3268 items 1 and 2 with K-3273: one identity per bound name. A parameter that holds a pattern has its own identity with the empty name, and the names its pattern binds are owned by it: the owner of an identity is the nearest actual identity-bearing declaration, with no lexical-scope exception. A variable declaration or binding element that holds a pattern has no identity, so the names it binds are owned by whatever encloses the declaration. A property selector is not a bound name
cases.note: { a, a: renamed } binds a and renamed: the second element's selector a is not a bound name, so there is no a#1. The element b: [c, d] and the element { f } hold patterns and have no identity. The pattern-holding parameter is pick#0/#0 and owns a, c, d and renamed; e and f are bound by a variable declaration that has no identity and are owned by the function

cases.name: member-name-sources
